title: Apply a function twice
description: Write a function `apply_twice(func, value)` that applies the function `func` to `value`, and then applies `func` again to that result, returning the final value. `func` will always be a one-argument function passed in by the caller.
hints: Functions can be passed around and called just like any other value in Python, including as arguments to another function.
You can call whatever function is stored in the `func` parameter by writing `func(...)`, the same way you'd call any other function.
Call `func(value)` first to get an intermediate result, then call `func` again on that intermediate result and return what that second call produces.
expected_behavior: Returns func(func(value)), i.e. func applied to value, and then func applied again to that result.
explanation: In Python, functions are first-class values, so `func` can be called just like any named function using `func(...)`. The inner call `func(value)` produces an intermediate result, and wrapping that in another `func(...)` call applies the same transformation a second time.
